chunks: Am I better than him who is contemptible, and cannot even express himself clearly?

key_terms.يُبِينُ: to express clearly, to make plain

ai.seo_question: Who is the 'contemptible' person mentioned in Surah Az-Zukhruf?
ai.summary: In this verse, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) rhetorically contrasts his divine mission and eloquence with the lowly status of a specific disbeliever, often identified by Shia exegetes as Ubay ibn Khalaf or a representative of the Quraysh elite, who struggled with clear speech. This comparison underscores the superiority of prophetic revelation over the mundane, inarticulate nature of worldly arrogance, serving as a critique of those who reject guidance despite their elevated social standing.
